sender.en: “Police”, “your bank’s fraud team” or a “recovery agency”

name.en: Recovery scam: “we can get back the money you lost to scammers”

how.en: After you lose money to a scam, especially if you posted about it online, someone contacts you offering to get it back. They claim to be police, your bank’s fraud team or a recovery company, or a fake profile says a recovery “expert” helped them. They ask for a fee, or send you to a website to “sign up” for the refund that asks for your bank login. They then take more of your money.

text.en: Someone contacts you after you lost money to a scam, sometimes after you posted about it online.
They say they are police, your bank or a recovery company, and that your money has been found.
They ask for a fee, or send you a link to a site that asks for your bank username and password.
They push you to act fast, then take more money.
Good news. Our recovery team has traced the funds you lost in the investment scam. To release your refund, register on our secure portal with your banking login: [link]
I saw your post about getting scammed. The same thing happened to me, and this recovery expert got all my money back. Message them today, they only take a few cases.

en: A stranger offers to get back money you lost to a scam.
They ask for a fee, tax or charge before the refund.
A refund website asks for your bank login.
They say they found you from your post about being scammed.
Don’t pay anyone who says they can recover lost money.
Never give your bank login on a website from a call, email or message.
Check by calling your bank or Police yourself on official numbers.
If you gave details, contact your bank straight away.
